title: Algorithmic management is associated with more work pressure and more access to learning
note: Cross-sectional employee reports, not longitudinal or causal evidence. Computer-based management can be conventional software rather than generative AI. Associations may reflect characteristics of more digitally advanced workplaces; under-35 is not an entry-level worker measure.

title: Managers perceive benefits and governance risks from algorithmic management
note: Employer/manager perception survey; not measured worker outcomes, firm performance, graduate hiring or generative AI deployment. Countries, survey designs and units differ from Eurofound; prevalence figures are not directly comparable.

title: Technical automation potential and projected adoption are not observed employment displacement
note: Technical feasibility, not observed adoption, labor displacement or learning outcomes. AI-mediated skill/activity mappings and optimistic workflow/value assumptions were not independently reproduced here. The appendix is part of this same research source, not a separate observation.

title: Organizational coordination may change employment and wages in non-linear ways
note: Stylized economic model with parameterized capability, coordination and competitive-market assumptions. No empirical test of youth outcomes, no forecast of dates or probability of structural shifts. Employment figures referenced in its literature discussion are not new independent observations.
